These proteins, in turn, are targets of other molecules that ultimately lead to the activation of Mcl-1. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with the highest score assigned to the pathway involving UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B17. This suggests that the interaction between Longistyline C and Mcl-1 may be part of a broader network of molecular interactions that influence cellular processes related to leukemia. The evidence is consistent across different pathways, but the exact nature of the interaction remains uncertain, as the direct link between Longistyline C and Mcl-1 is not explicitly established. The observed scores reflect the strength of the evidence, but further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the biological relevance of these findings.
